findings.description: F004 says each integration emits two items, but F001 requires one ActionItem per catalog action step. Firebase functions has separate credential and deploy steps, so a two-items-per-integration rule would either collapse distinct pending actions or conflict with the completion test's one-truthful-ActionItem-per-step requirement.
findings.recommendation: Pin cardinality as one STATUS item per integration plus one ACTION item per unresolved catalog action row, with firebase-creds and firebase-deploy clearing independently.

findings.description: The Firebase trigger is defined as action_id firebase-trigger, but the catalog does not make it a visible operator action or otherwise provide the exact attestation command that satisfies the trigger. The operator can see the gated deploy/realtime items but lacks a first-class, rendered path to mark multi-operator need as met.
findings.recommendation: Add either a catalog row for firebase-trigger or require the gated items to render the exact trigger attestation command and evidence expectation, then test the trigger-unmet to trigger-met transition through rendered output.

findings.description: F003 intentionally renders trigger-unmet deploy/realtime items as info, and F004 renders status items as info, but the shipped operator-console triage path treats info/advisory as quiet and the default console only shows needs_auth, needs_decision, and uncertain. The plan does not pin how these always-visible integration items appear in the standard operator-console surface.
findings.recommendation: Specify the operator-console model and renderer changes that keep integration info/status items visible without promoting them to needs_action, and cover that path with fixture-render tests.

findings.description: The render-proof smoke says it runs the real dashboard build over export-dashboard output and checks built rendered artifacts, but it does not pin the actual render mechanism. For a static SPA, copied state JSON and static build output can diverge from browser-rendered DOM, so the smoke could remain parse-proof rather than render-proof.
findings.recommendation: Pin the smoke to a concrete offline render path, such as building/exporting state, loading the dashboard with that state in a headless browser or equivalent DOM renderer, and asserting identifying values in the rendered page output.

findings.description: The status matrix says a later failed record surfaces a failure flag without regressing the status floor, but it does not define record ordering or malformed-record handling. Captured timestamps, JSONL append order, duplicate records, and unknown action_ids can produce different derived statuses unless the deterministic rule is pinned.
findings.recommendation: Define JSONL append order as the history order, require attestation writes to reject unknown integration/action pairs, and add matrix fixtures for duplicate, out-of-order timestamp, malformed, and failed-after-passed records.
